newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian share bull-run charges to record high.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian share bull-run charges to record high.

text.p: Slovenian shares extended their spectacular bull run on Thursday with the blue-chip index soaring to a record close for the second day in a row.
The SBI index ended 28.20 points, or 1.74 percent, higher at 1,650.58 -- chalking up a 39.3 percent gain since the beginning of the year.
Traders said that while market sentiment remained decidedly bullish, the market was due for a correction to consolidate the recent gains.
"As it looks now the SBI index could grow a further 10 percent in the near future. But I expect the index to stabilise over the next week," said Darja Kos Godec at brokers Poteza.

Today's gains were largely fed by continued demand for drug maker Lek, traders said. Lek's A issue jumped 7.03 percent to 33,930 tolars on volume of 9,023 shares, while Lek's C issue soared 8.06 percent to 33,500 tolars.
Future market direction hinges on whether foreign investors, the driving force behind the tiny Alpine republic's bull run, continue to snap up stocks or decide to cash in profits, traders said.

"The upward trend will continue as long as foreigners are prepared to continue buying shares of Lek...but when they stop buying, the index could tumble 30 to 50 percent," Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka, said.
Turnover ballooned to 877.2 million tolars from 598.9 million on Wednesday. Overall 15 shares rose, four fell and six were untraded.
"The market is full of optimism and I think shares could continue rising over the next week, especially after Krka is listed," one trader said.
Pharmaceutical producer Krka, the main rival of Lek, will list its shares on the over-the-counter market on Monday.
Traders said the eagerly-anticipated London listing of bank SKB's global depositary receipts was a further trading incentive for investors to chew on.
SKB was the most actively traded in today's session but fell prey to profit-taking and shed 1.24 percent to 75,950 tolars on volume of 5,932 shares.
Sources close to the bank said they expected the listing to go ahead next week.
